question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: Ensuring no harm comes to the patient or nurse during the procedure
options.B: Reducing the overall cost of purchasing hospital medical supplies
options.C: Speeding up the time it takes to administer daily medication rounds
options.D: Eliminating the need to wear gloves when handling clean syringes

explanation: Injection safety focuses entirely on protecting both recipients and healthcare providers from physical harm and infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why do nurses carry a major responsibility in maintaining injection safety?

options.A: They purchase all medical equipment used in the healthcare facility
options.B: They are responsible for manufacturing sterile needles in the hospital
options.C: They dictate the national health policies regarding infectious waste
options.D: They are the primary healthcare workers who administer injections to patients

explanation: Nurses are directly responsible for preparing and administering injections, placing them at the center of safety protocol execution. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h1)

question: When does the practice of injection safety actually begin?

options.A: Washing the patient's entire body with antibacterial soap and water
options.B: Recapping the needle tightly to ensure it stays sterile on the tray
options.C: Notifying the hospital director of the intended medication route
options.D: Deciding if an injection is truly necessary compared to oral medication

explanation: Think of safety as starting before you even pick up a syringe. If a patient can take oral medication instead, avoiding that needle prick is the safest first step! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which of these best captures the full picture of injection safety?

options.A: It is limited to washing hands before opening a packaged syringe
options.B: It covers everything from deciding on the route to safe disposal of waste
options.C: It focuses solely on preventing needlestick injuries among medical doctors
options.D: It only refers to the exact moment the needle enters the patient's skin

explanation: Injection safety isn't just one quick action. It's a complete journey—from checking if the injection is needed, to giving it cleanly, to throwing away the sharps properly. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h2)

question: What dangerous practice must nurses avoid to protect themselves from needlestick injuries?
explanation: Recapping used needles is a primary cause of accidental needlestick injuries in clinical settings and must be avoided. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h3)

question: A nurse finishes giving an intramuscular injection to a patient. What is the safest immediate action regarding the used syringe?

options.A: Place the cap back on the needle using two hands before walking to the bin
options.B: Break the needle off the syringe by hand to save space in the disposal box
options.C: Drop the unsheathed needle and syringe directly into a rigid sharps container
options.D: Leave the syringe on the bedside table until the end of the shift

explanation: Immediate disposal of the unsheathed device into a puncture-resistant container prevents accidental injuries to staff and patients. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which bloodborne viruses are most commonly transmitted through unsafe injection practices?

options.D: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

explanation: Unsafe injections are a major vector for transmitting bloodborne infections like Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h4)

question: How do painful abscesses and bacterial infections usually happen after an injection?

options.A: Due to the natural chemical reaction of the medication inside the blood
options.B: As a normal side effect of every vaccine given in the muscle
options.C: Because the patient did not take oral antibiotics before the injection
options.D: Through contaminated equipment or poor skin preparation introducing bacteria

explanation: Abscesses happen when germs get introduced into the skin or muscle. This is why thorough hand washing, clean gear, and proper skin wiping are so important! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main reason we practice standard precautions in everyday nursing?

options.A: To prevent the transmission of infections between patients and staff
options.B: To ensure medications dissolve faster in the patient's bloodstream
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital cleaning supplies
options.D: To eliminate the need for documenting medication administration

explanation: Standard precautions are your trusty shield! They keep both you and your patients safe from passing germs back and forth during care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h5)

question: How should a nurse properly clean a medication vial septum before drawing up fluid?

options.A: Blow air heavily onto the rubber top to cool and clean it
options.B: Wipe the rubber top with an alcohol swab and allow it to dry
options.C: Wipe the top with a dry paper towel immediately before insertion
options.D: Run the entire glass bottle under hot tap water for one minute

explanation: Swabbing the septum with alcohol and letting it dry naturally reduces surface bacteria prior to needle insertion. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h5)

question: What key physical features must a proper sharps container have?

options.A: Transparent and open at the top

explanation: Sharps bins have to be tough! Being puncture-resistant and leak-proof ensures that needles won't poke through and fluids won't spill out while waiting for disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h6)

question: What action should a nurse take when a sharps container reaches its designated fill line?

options.A: Leave it open on the counter until the end of the working week
options.B: Seal and close the container securely for safe disposal
options.C: Push the needles down firmly with a gloved hand to create more space
options.D: Transfer some of the used needles into a regular plastic trash bag

explanation: Containers must be closed and replaced once they reach the fill line to prevent accidental overflows and needle injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h6)
